findings.reason: a node building to this case either fails its own done-when or quietly narrows it, and the coordinator never learns which.
findings.text: §7's first case is a log holding a failing run then a passing run whose `after_suite` arm carries the first run's failure count and ids, and it requires the refusal to name "the count and the ids"; but `review.gate_log_failure_ids` returns exactly the first run's ids for that log (verified: `['tests/one.py::a']` on `2 failed … / FAILED tests/one.py::a / EXIT=1 / 261 passed … / EXIT=0`), so the id comparison passes and no id is named, leaving only the count mismatch

findings.reason: the section must name a last-run id reader (or the case must swap its runs so the stale arm names ids the log's last run does not), otherwise the mechanism that this section exists to add is not the mechanism it describes.
findings.text: the deliverable says the check "reads the log's last run, the one the exit status is read from" and then names `review_module.gate_log_failure_ids` for the ids, but that function scans every `FAILED`/`ERROR` line in the whole text (`reckon/crew/review.py:2069–2074`) and neither `promotion_evidence.py` nor `review.py` carries a reader that cuts the log at its last run — the cited power_convertor helper avoids the problem only because its doubled log has a *passing* first run, which contributes no `FAILED` lines

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every in-repo anchor lands at the line it names (`promotion_release.py` 337/476/633, `crew_run_commands.py` 3179, `merge.py` 783–793, `promotion_evidence.py` 1044/1062/1174, `review.py` 2106), and the three external anchors resolve (the worktree-withholding note, investigation run `r-20261106T193257319275-a-merged-landing-withholds-its-worktree`, and `power_convertor tests/test_plant_owner.py:326` `_receipt_mismatches`).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §7's first case requires a doubled log to be refused "naming the count and the ids", but the id comparison the same section specifies matches on exactly that log, so the ids half of the case cannot be satisfied.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §6 requires every log under the run directory with a revision header and a closing `EXIT=` line; §7's temporary logs are test fixtures rather than gate evidence, and nothing in either unit writes to a session scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §6 and §7 name no plan label, ticket number or version tag in any symbol, file or comment they ask for; their section references stay in plan prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §7's stated mechanism reads the cited log's failure ids with `review_module.gate_log_failure_ids`, which scans the whole log rather than the last run the deliverable says it reads, so the mechanism cannot produce the id mismatch §7 asserts. §6's root cause is verified against the code and holds: the post-merge release is computed and then discarded in favour of the pre-merge receipt.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §6 states one behaviour (a landed head releases its worktree) with one gate and two causes, and §7 states one behaviour (a receipt's failure figures agree with its log); each closes on one verdict.
